records.question: Where does the UN's AI and digital-technology build-out stand?
records.answer: Of the 12 layers the UNGA81 package tracks (as of September 30, 2026), 3 are operating (Mandate and focal point; Evidence, dialogue and implementation lab; Capacity centres and diffusion network), 6 are under way, 2 are proposed only and 1 is only a panel that was held. The money is not there yet: the Secretary-General proposes a $3 billion starting fund and the September 21 closed design session was held; no governing or capitalization instrument was located at cutoff. Cross-border AI sandboxes: the Valencia Lab operates and the September 21 co-design session was held, but no public charter, standards work item, shared-protocol network or pilot was located. Tokenization as public infrastructure: the September 21 panel was held; Pakistan publicly framed tokenization around remittances, SME finance, sovereign debt, access, safeguards and standards participation, while no UN standard, legal model or pilot was located.

records.question: What did the 2026 UN General Assembly week actually produce?
records.answer: Of 9 outcomes tracked from the week (September 18, 2026 to September 29, 2026), 1 was adopted (Sea-level rise declaration), 1 published, 2 held with no outcome document yet, 2 still under way and 2 only proposed (Global AI capacity fund; Cross-border AI sandbox network). The Durban anniversary declaration is past due: its meeting has passed and the library has no record of adoption. No AI fund, sandbox network or UN tokenization model was set up.

records.question: What has the U.S. government done abroad with sanctions and money since 2025?
records.answer: The world record holds 12 U.S. government actions since 2025 that changed money abroad, February 26, 2025 to June 1, 2026: sanctions and takedowns aimed at Russia's crypto routes and Venezuela's oil, a Section 301 trade case against Brazil's Pix payment system, a $20 billion Treasury swap line for Argentina, a tariff deal with Indonesia, a U.S.-UK markets taskforce and the G20 boycott. 5 rest on a U.S. government document; the other 7 link news or law-firm pages and are marked 'needs primary source'.

records.question: Which international bodies has the U.S. left, and when does each exit take effect?
records.answer: The U.S. has fully left 1 body: the Paris Agreement (effective January 27, 2026). Its exit from the World Health Organization is claimed effective January 22, 2026 but disputed: WHO still treated the U.S. as a member in arrears in May 2026. UNESCO exit takes effect December 31, 2026. The parent UN climate treaty (UNFCCC) exit takes effect February 27, 2027. On February 3, 2025 it stopped taking part in the UN Human Rights Council and cut its money to UNRWA, without leaving the UN. For 10 other bodies an exit clause exists but no U.S. notice was found.

records.question: What does the U.S. pay, and how does it vote, in each international body?
records.answer: The U.S. share runs from 49.99% (Organization of American States, 2026 assessed quota) down to 9.09% (ITER, construction sharing baseline). At the UN it pays 22% of the regular budget and 26.1371% of peacekeeping, but still has one Assembly vote. Paying more buys more votes only where votes are weighted by money, at the IMF and World Bank: the U.S. IMF share can block decisions requiring 85% of total voting power; IBRD influence derives from shareholding.

records.question: What can the U.S. block or decide in each international body, and what can't it?
records.answer: Across 27 bodies, U.S. power sits in five different places: a veto, consensus seat or blocking share in 5 (United Nations, NATO, International Monetary Fund, ITER, Board of Peace), money leverage in 8, domestic implementation in 8, command or facility access in 5 and agenda power in 6. A gate can stop specified action but does not give command: at the UN Security Council, procedural matters require nine votes and are not vetoable; affirmative action still needs nine votes.
